how: Paved and forested ridge trail linking Mount Faber to Kent Ridge, about 9-10 km, with NParks guided walks also offered.
Permit-based tent camping at designated campsites (Jelutong, Mamam, Endut Senin) on Pulau Ubin; other legal sites exist but are few.
Shorebird and mangrove birding at Sungei Buloh; Nature Society Bird Group runs walks (membership/account needed).
Light-polluted city, but Science Centre Observatory runs public telescope nights and amateurs hold star parties at East Coast Park; weather and haze limit it.
NParks leases small allotment plots in parks (ballot when oversubscribed); also community gardens via Community in Bloom.
Guided walks over the Chek Jawa intertidal flats at low spring tide; NParks tours reported suspended for maintenance and bookings are competitive.
Park-based orienteering races and O-training run by the Orienteering Federation Singapore; mostly urban parks, no real forest. Sources are 2018-2019, so current activity unverified.
Hundreds to 1,000+ caches island-wide, from parks to malls, via the Geocaching app.
Plant collecting is prohibited in nature reserves; the nearest legal version is a guided edible-plant foraging tour of rooftop farms in the City Hall area.
venue: Edible Garden City (Raffles City / Funan urban farms)

how: Rod fishing allowed in marked zones, e.g. the Jurong Lake recreational jetty (artificial bait only), plus free spots like the Changi boardwalk.
Nature Society Butterfly & Insect Group runs regular walks at reservoir parks and the Botanic Gardens.
Free NParks Nature Appreciation Walks at Bukit Timah Nature Reserve, about an hour, registration required.
Ketam Mountain Bike Park and dirt trails on Pulau Ubin; bikes rentable at the jetty (some rentals bar the Ketam trails).
Compacted forest trails around MacRitchie Reservoir (about 11 km loop) and the Rail Corridor.
250 m suspension bridge about 25 m above the forest floor in MacRitchie, reached by a long forest trail; opening days vary by source.
Hands-on tabletop hydroponics workshops at a high-tech vertical farm; also rooftop farm tours and volunteer sessions (ComCrop).
Few natural crags in Singapore; climbing is almost entirely indoors at dozens of bouldering and wall gyms (e.g. Climb Central, Onsight).
Little commercial farmland left and no pick-your-own orchard culture; farm tours exist but no public fruit picking was verified.
Removing plants, fungi or animals from parks and nature reserves is prohibited, and there is no seasonal forest-foraging culture.
Swimming in reservoirs, rivers and most waterways is generally prohibited; swimming is limited to beaches and pools.
Migratory raptors pass through Sept-April and peregrine falcons are seen on tall buildings; NParks biodiversity pages document them.
No public beekeeping course or hive-keeping opportunity was found; not verified either way.
No desert or ice fields to search; meteorites are only in museum or dealer hands.
Operators and informal groups reportedly run ghost-story night walks, but no verified single provider was found.
Vertical wind tunnel in Sentosa: briefing plus two short flights with an instructor; simulated, not a real jump.
About 50 m tower on Siloso Beach with a few seconds of freefall and optional pool dip.
No drop zone for civilian skydiving was found in Singapore; real jumps are overseas (e.g. Malaysia, Thailand, New Zealand).
No cliffs or structures that can legally be jumped, and airspace and building rules are strict.
Tropical climate with no natural snow; nearest real slopes are in Japan or Korea.
Indoor conveyor-style ski/snowboard simulator with coach-led lessons (listed at the EU Holidays Expo, Raffles Boulevard).
Snow City, the indoor snow centre near Science Centre, was reported (Wikipedia) to close on 30 Sep 2026; closure not confirmed on operator site, recheck.
No game hunting: wildlife is protected and civilian firearm possession is tightly restricted under the Arms and Explosives Act.
No wild big game, but the Night Safari and Singapore Zoo offer a captive-wildlife tram and walking experience.
MegaZip drops about 450 m from Imbiah Hill toward Siloso Beach at around 60 km/h.
Wheeled gravity cart luge on four tracks at Sentosa's Imbiah Lookout, not an ice luge.
Cable-ski lagoon with beginner-friendly cable systems for wakeboarding and water-skiing, gear included.
No natural cave systems or karst; only WWII tunnels with no public caving.
No flooded caves; nearest cave-diving sites are in Malaysia, Mexico or Florida.
No glaciers or ice fields within thousands of kilometres.
No natural ice and no known ice-climbing wall in Singapore.
No volcanoes in Singapore; nearest are in Indonesia.
No bullfighting or bull-running tradition, and animal-cruelty laws would prohibit it.
No rodeo circuit or livestock culture in Singapore.
No public hands-on falconry experience was found; birds of prey appear only in zoo or bird-park shows.
No suitable hills or flight clearance; flying sites are in Malaysia and elsewhere.
No regular civilian free-flight balloon operator found in Singapore.
No rivers with rapids; nearest rafting is in Malaysia.
No canyons or gorges in Singapore.
No snow or sled-dog culture.
No dunes or desert; only beach sand.
Multi-level aerial obstacle courses at Mega Adventure Park (Sentosa); specific course not verified.
Licensed clubs such as SAFRA Shooting Club and Singapore Gun Club offer trap/skeet but access is limited; laser clay shooting is the open alternative.
venue: SAFRA Shooting Club / Singapore Gun Club

how: Highest point is Bukit Timah Hill (163 m); real mountaineering needs trips to Malaysia, Nepal or beyond, though climbing gyms help training.
